method: Questions were researched with an evidence-only retrieval tool over one corpus of open-access and public-domain texts (see corpus.json). Each excerpt was checked word for word against the corpus passage it cites when this file was written; corpus_chunk numbers that passage in the corpus snapshot of 2026-10-01.
questions: What is the prototype theory of concepts, and where did it come from?
How does it explain typicality effects?
Where does the prototype theory struggle?
What alternatives and combinations have been proposed?

evidence.excerpt: According to this theory, a lexical concept C doesn’t have definitional structure but has probabilistic structure in that something falls under C just in case it satisfies a sufficient number of properties encoded by C’s constituents.
it has its psychological roots in Eleanor Rosch’s groundbreaking experimental treatment of much the same idea
the reason apples are judged to be more typical than plums is that the concept APPLE shares more of its constituents with FRUIT
One is that its treatment of categorization works best for quick and unreflective judgments.
If asked whether a dog that is surgically altered to look like a raccoon is a dog or a raccoon, the answer for most of us, and even for children, is that it is remains a dog
PET FISH encodes properties such as brightly colored, which have no basis in the prototype structure for either PET or FISH
many patently complex concepts don’t even have a prototype structure (e.g., CHAIRS THAT WERE PURCHASED ON A WEDNESDAY)
One general solution that addresses all of these problems is to hold that a prototype constitutes just part of the structure of a concept.
This is the view that concepts stand in relation to one another in the same way as the terms of a scientific theory
claiming that even children are in possession of a rudimentary biological theory. This theory tells them that being a dog isn’t just a matter of looking like a dog.
One problem that has been raised against the theory theory is that it has difficulty in allowing for different people to possess the same concepts
there is no reason why philosophers shouldn’t maintain that concepts have different types of structure
These same considerations have led some theorists to advocate concept eliminativism—the view that there are no concepts (Machery 2009).
concept should be understood to be a natural kind if concepts exist at all
from an emphasis on definition and analysis to ‘family resemblance’ and ‘language-games’
later Wittgenstein can be summed up as the total rejection of dogmatism
